why:
The quote is real and the cited lines say what was claimed, but the CONSEQUENCE is false and was measured false — the repo's recurring 'the identifier is unwired, but something upstream already handled it' shape, compounded by the finding naming the wrong field (frontmatter `name`) in the wrong subsystem.

1. DOC — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md` -> 1250 lines, 94956 bytes, md5 cf7b0c7d5ff8adff60f6a174cd6938f4. The claimed string is an exact substring of line 277 (checked in Python, not by eye). Reading the WHOLE line changes nothing against the finding — it reinforces it: `| `name` | Yes | Unique identifier using lowercase letters and hyphens. [Hooks](/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart) receive this value as `agent_type`. The filename doesn't have to match. {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}Names can't contain `:`, which is reserved for [plugin-scoped identifiers](/docs/en/plugins) such as `my-plugin:reviewer`. Claude Code doesn't load a file whose name contains one and logs an error to the debug log. Before v2.1.218, such names were accepted |`. So the doc half stands, and the rule is version-gated at v2.1.218.

2. FILE — CONFIRMED AS WRITTEN, all four citations. `packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283` is exactly `normalizeName(name) { return name.trim().toLowerCase(); }` with no character validation. `:725-726` is exactly `defs.find(def => def.name === normalized) ?? defs.find(def => def.aliases?.includes(normalized))`. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:250-264` `qualifiedKey` does `.join('::')`. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:153-154` is `name: hasUnqualifiedAlias ? descriptor.name : descriptor.key` / `aliases: [...new Set([descriptor.key, ...])]`. There is no colon check anywhere in the agents subsystem (`grep -ran` over `packages/shared/src/agents/` and `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/` for `includes(':')`, `indexOf(':')`, `/:/`, `[a-z0-9-]`, `colon`: zero non-test hits).

3. CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED ON THREE INDEPENDENT GROUNDS.

(a) The stated exploit path is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: markdown definitions and runtime (plugin-key-bearing) definitions are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. `loadAgentDefinitions` guards the entire markdown block with `if (options.runtimeDefinitions === undefined)` (definitions.ts:670-684) and only then appends `options.runtimeDefinitions ?? []` (:686). Plugin capability keys reach this function ONLY as runtime definitions, so in any load where a plugin key exists, no workspace/project markdown file has been read at all. Every production caller supplies the field and never leaves it `undefined`: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:513` and `workflow-tool.ts:591` both pass `options.getRuntimeAgentDefinitions?.() ?? []`, and `review-tool.ts:300` passes `[]`.

MEASURED, with a positive control (an ABSENCE needs one):
  CONTROL (runtimeDefinitions omitted): a workspace `reviewer.md` DOES override the built-in -> systemPrompt "I AM THE OVERRIDE."   <- the rig can see shadowing
  PROD SHAPE (runtimeDefinitions: []): same file on disk -> systemPrompt "You are a reviewer agent. Focu…"  <- markdown never loaded
  IMPOSTOR TEST: workspace `impostor.md` with frontmatter `name: "agent::plugin::-::-::::reviewer"` alongside a runtime definition whose definitionKey is that same string -> `resolveAgentDefinition('agent::plugin::-::-::::reviewer')` returns "I am the REAL plugin agent." The impostor is absent from the map entirely.

(b) The finding names the WRONG FIELD for the path that carries plugin keys. In the capability/runtime pipeline an agent is named by its FILENAME, not by frontmatter `name`: `native-sources.ts:332` `const logicalName = entry.name.replace(/\.md$/i, '')`, and the runtime binding is `resolver.ts:965` `agent: { key, name: record.logicalName, … }` for native agents and `resolver.ts:1245` `name: candidate.logicalName` for plugin agents; the descriptor then carries `name: agent.name` (`pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:643`). The frontmatter `name` key is read only by `definitions.ts`'s own parser (`parseMarkdownAgentDefinition:534-536`) — i.e. exactly and only in the fallback path where, per (a), no plugin key can be present. So "a workspace or project markdown agent file may DECLARE a colon-bearing name equal to a plugin's capability key" cannot happen: in the path that has plugin keys, the declaration is ignored.

(c) The reservation's RATIONALE does not transfer. Claude reserves `:` because its plugin-scoped reference syntax is literally `my-plugin:reviewer`. This fork implements no such syntax — a plugin-scoped agent is referenced by its opaque `::`-joined qualified key or by its short logical name, and nothing else: `base-agent.ts:2557` (`candidate.key === agent || (candidate.selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias && candidate.name === agent)`) and `runtime-agent-definition.ts:224-225` (`value.key === reference` ?? `value.logicalName === reference`). A single `:` is therefore not a namespace separator here and cannot collide with one.

Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` (read all nine: SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries — none touches agent name validation). Not a rebrand or a subscription-drop difference either. It is refuted on measurement, not on category.
correctedState: What survives is a narrow hygiene divergence with no security or shadowing consequence: `normalizeName` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283) only trims and lowercases, so a markdown subagent file that declares a colon-bearing frontmatter `name` LOADS instead of being refused — measured: both `has:colon` and `agent::plugin::-::-::::reviewer` load with zero entries in `onInvalidDefinition`, whereas Claude Code v2.1.218+ skips such a file and logs to the debug log. The finding's impersonation consequence is false. A markdown-declared name can never shadow a plugin capability key, because `loadAgentDefinitions` reads markdown ONLY when `options.runtimeDefinitions === undefined` (:670-684) and plugin keys arrive exclusively as runtime definitions, while every production caller passes the field (subagent-tool.ts:513, workflow-tool.ts:591, review-tool.ts:300). Independently, the capability path names native and plugin agents by `logicalName` — filename or plugin component name (native-sources.ts:332, resolver.ts:965 and :1245) — and ignores frontmatter `name` entirely, so the declaration the finding relies on is not read on that path. And `:` is not a namespace separator in this fork at all: there is no `plugin:agent` reference form, only the opaque `::`-joined qualified key or the short logical name (base-agent.ts:2557, runtime-agent-definition.ts:224-225). The `name`-before-`aliases` order at :725-726 is real but not exploitable through the claimed route. Residual work, if any, is cosmetic parity: reject `:` in `normalizeName` and report it through the existing per-file `onInvalidDefinition` skip.
